texts: Operative mortality is highest when an older recipient receives an older donor heart after a long ischaemic time: E.
Recipient age, donor age and ischaemic time each add risk, and their effects add up: the grandfather, the weathered hotel and the hourglass that ran out, beside the biggest coffin.
A young recipient with a young donor heart and a short ischaemic time carries the lowest risk.
Older donor hearts tolerate long ischaemic times, beyond about four hours, less well.
Memory hook: old with old, after a long wait on ice, fills the biggest coffin.
